confidence_notes: I did three of the six allowed web searches: one for the RBA rate and two for Rome food and drink prices. They did not reach Numbeo's own Rome page. The figures I found came from secondary sites quoting Numbeo or Expatistan and from guides. They varied a lot: one source gave $22 for a mid-range dinner for two, which looks too low. I used these results together with general knowledge of Rome menu prices, at a working rate of about 1 EUR = 1.10 USD. The beer, wine and cocktail figures are for typical restaurants and bars in the central or tourist areas. Neighbourhood bars charge less (about EUR 4-5 for a pint, EUR 6-7 for a cocktail and EUR 1.50-3 for basic house wine), and the central and tourist areas charge about EUR 8-12 for wine and EUR 10-12 or more for cocktails. Expatistan's figure of about EUR 11 for a cocktail rests on few data points. The coffee figure assumes a standing cappuccino at a bar, about EUR 1.70. Sitting at a table, especially in tourist areas, can cost a lot more. The accommodation figures are general estimates for peak July demand, not checked against any booking pages or listings, and are the least certain anchors. Rome's per-person city tax may not be fully reflected.
comparable_city_reasoning: Mainly Rome-specific secondary and aggregated figures, checked against other major Western European tourist capitals such as Barcelona, Florence and Milan. Rome is high-demand in July. Its food prices are moderate for Western Europe, but its hotel prices are high in peak season.
